content:
alex_dev: Hey team, heads-up — Enterprise customer 'NimbleSearch' is hitting intermittent 400s when sending batched embedding requests through our TS aggregator (they call our Python SDK which hits hosted API). They see 'embedding dimension mismatch' logs and a large number of retries.
alex_dev: Quick summary: Python client sends batch of 8 texts, TS aggregator forwards as single request to /v1/embeddings. About 1 in 5 requests returns 400 with payload:

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error": "Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024"}
```

alex_dev: Customer repro attached (they say it happens reliably under load). They also reported spikes in token billing because our client retries were configured to retry on 4xx in their infra. Oof.

maria_support: Thanks Alex — can you paste the minimal repro script? Also need the exact SDK versions (python/ts) and model name they were calling. Did they pin model to a variant? :thinking:

alex_dev: Sure — they provided this small script (Python):

```
# requirements: redwood==0.9.3
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
c = EmbeddingsClient(api_key="sk-xxxx")
texts = ["short text"]*8
resp = c.create(model="open-embed-1536", input=texts, batch_size=8, timeout=10)
print(resp)
```

alex_dev: On the TS side they aggregate multiple user requests into one larger batch and set `Content-Type: application/json` and pass through the `model` field from the client. TS aggregator is at 1.4.1. They confirmed the forwarded body looks fine.

samir_ml: Possible causes: model metadata mismatch (model actually serving 1024 dim but client expects 1536), or upstream model variant routing during autoscaling changed model instance (e.g., fallback to quantized smaller variant) without updating advertised dim. Another thought: partial batching where some items come from a different model call due to multi-tenant routing bug.

samir_ml: Can you grab a raw server-side log from the inference runtime for a failing request? I want the model_name, model_variant, and the embedding vector length we returned. If we returned 1024, that's the kernel/model variant issue. If we returned 1536 but client says 1024, maybe the python sdk is truncating/reading incorrectly.

alex_dev: Attached logs showed: `model=open-embed-1536 variant=quantized-v2 dims=1024` for one of the failing requests. So runtime reported 1024.

chloe_prod: That suggests we routed to quantized-v2 which is a 1024-dim variant. We should never advertise `open-embed-1536` pointing to a 1024 variant. This likely originates in our smart routing / fallback logic where a capacity-constrained node returned a smaller-quantized variant with different vocab dims. Need quick mitigation: stop auto-fallback for that model family.

maria_support: For the customer immediate mitigation: ask them to set batch_size=1 or explicitly set `model: open-embed-1536@v1` (pin exact version) in the request. Also recommend they turn off client-side retries for 4xx while we investigate. I'll send a templated message asking them to pin model + disable 4xx retries.

alex_dev: Customer also asked about billing — they saw duplicate charges from retries. They want a partial refund while this is investigated.

maria_support: I'll open a billing docket and mark it P1. Please include a log sample and approximate wasted token count. We can request finance to issue credit.

samir_ml: Engineering fix plan: 1) Add a check in the routing layer to verify model metadata `embedding_dim` matches the requested model's expected dim before returning; 2) Disable automatic fallback to variants with mismatched dims; 3) Add active regression tests that validate dim invariants for each model alias.

chloe_prod: Short term hotfix: I'll push config to the control plane to disable fallback for `open-embed-1536` alias. Rolling out now. Expect <5m. infra-bot: can you post rollout status? \
infra-bot: Deploy started: control-plane-config-2026-09-05T13:22Z. Canary to 2 nodes. Rolling back on failure.

infra-bot: Canary OK on node-a, node-b. Rollout complete to 3/3 pools.

chloe_prod: Hotfix applied. Can we confirm with the customer? Alexa, can you ask them to run the repro with batch_size=8 again and paste the server log (or we can pull server-side logs for their request id)?

alex_dev: Reached out — they ran test after hotfix, and initial results: no 400s for ~50 requests, but one 400 popped up after a load spike. Log for that one shows `model=router-proxy variant=quantized-v2 dims=1024`.

samir_ml: Hmm still a router-proxy path choosing quantized-v2. We need to trace request route id -> node decision. I think there's a stale mapping in the router cache that didn't refresh on config push.

samir_ml: Action: I'll request the router cache be invalidated. Also adding extra logging to include `alias_resolved_to: <model_variant>` in future.

maria_support: Customer asked for a reproducible snippet that avoids the problem while we fix infra. I suggested `batch_size=4` and client timeout increased to 30s and `retry_policy: { on_4xx: false, on_5xx: true, backoff: exponential_jitter }`. They agreed to try.

alex_dev: Provided a TS aggregator patch to set `max_batch=4` and not retry 4xx; they deployed that patch.

chloe_prod: Router cache invalidate done. Monitoring for next hour.

infra-bot: Router cache purge submitted: job-7782.

alex_dev: Customer just reported that setting batch_size=4 eliminated the 400s so far during a 30-min test. They also accepted temporary credit while we audit token duplication. Maria — any updates on billing?

maria_support: Billing ticket created: BILL-2041. Asking finance for emergency credit of ~2k USD pending final audit.

samir_ml: Longer-term: we should add server-side validation that rejects requests where requested embedding dimension (from model alias metadata) != served dim, and return 409 with clear message indicating alias mismatch, not 400. Also add an SDK-level guard — when model alias meta is fetched, validate `embedding_dim` and warn if mismatch.

chloe_prod: Agreed. I'll create a GH issue in eng-runtime repo and tag eng-ml.

chloe_prod: Issue: https://github.com/redwood/eng-runtime/issues/512 (created) — title: 'Prevent mismatched embedding dimensions due to fallback routing' — assigned to @samir_ml.

samir_ml: I'll pick it up. Plan: 1) Add metadata check in router; 2) Add invariant test in onboarding harness; 3) Emit metric `router_dim_mismatch_count` and alert if > 0 in 5m window.

maria_support: Next steps for support: keep customer on batch_size=4 or pinned variant, pause 4xx retries, and confirm credit. I'll follow up once finance confirms.

alex_dev: One more note for SDK folks — in Python SDK we should not treat all 4xx as non-retryable by default (we should) but if their retry middleware is misconfigured it retried 400 which caused duplicate billing. We should improve SDK docs and default config: no retries on 4xx, clear example using `retry.on_status = [429, 503]`.

chloe_prod: Good call. @samir_ml please make sure runtime returns distinct error codes for alias mismatch (409) vs bad payload (400) so SDKs can make correct decisions.

samir_ml: Will do. I'll also add an integration test that simulates multi-variant fallback and asserts the router refuses to route to variant with different dims.

maria_support: I'll send a final message to the customer summarizing the mitigations (hotfix, router purge, suggested client changes, billing credit in progress).

alex_dev: Thanks all. I'll keep monitoring. If anyone sees additional 400s, ping #eng-runtime and I'll forward logs. :+1:
